ucldc_schema:description.item: An oral history with Mr. Charlie Van Le, a graduate of University of Texas at Austin where he majored in Asian Studies and minored in Asian American Studies. This interview focused on his experiences as a second generation Vietnamese American growing up without learning much about his family’s experiences in Vietnam, during the war, and with migration. He is volunteering with the 500 Oral Histories Project in order to help preserve that history.

In 2008, the Vietnamese American community in Austin, along with VAHF, successfully collaborated with the University of Texas at Austin’s Center For Asian American Studies (CAAS) to establish a course on Vietnamese American history and culture, instructed by Ph.D. candidate Linda Ho Peché. Each student was required to complete an oral interview of a self-identified Vietnamese American. These oral histories became part of the 500 Oral History Project initiated by VAHF as its third most urgent collection, since many members of the first genera- tion of Vietnamese Americans are now elderly. With their passing, first-hand accounts of the Vietnamese American immigration experience would be lost.

ucldc_schema:description.item: Avionne Hernandez is a young mother of a two year old girl from the rural village of Brasso Seco, Paria, Trinidad, who comes from a family of farmers. She shares that her parents were not happy when they learned she was expecting a baby. They put her out of the house and she went to live with boyfriend. She accessed health care at the Sangre Grande Hospital. She says her pregnancy was easy, the only negative side effect being the stretch marks she remained with after giving. She recounts her experience delivering her daughter and adjusting to breastfeeding and caring for her baby after birth. She also talks about her daughter's personality.

ucldc_schema:description.item: This video produced by the LA Alliance for a New Economy documents elements of the Living Wage campaign in Los Angeles. An actor dressed as the ghost of Jacob Marley from Charles Dickens' "A Christmas Carol" haunts LA's city hall, warning the mayor and council members to consider the needs of low wage workers in December 1996. The video also includes interviews with activists following a successful vote in the council in March 1997. The ordinance covered workers city contractors.

ucldc_schema:description.item: Jeuel Scott is a 41 year old mother of four children. She has been in Tobago for three years. Her first child was born in Trinidad and the rest in Tobago. She recalls the delivery of each of her children. Her first child was born at the Mt. Hope Maternity Hospital in Trinidad after twenty-two hours of labour. Her last pregnancy was physically traumatic and the baby was delivered via C-section. She spent weeks at the hospital recovering and the last child was kept for observation.

ucldc_schema:description.item: Stephanie Dumm is 38 years old. She has a B.A. in Journalism, which she was only able to use for three years as a journalist for a local newspaper “The Lincoln Messenger” before she quit to be a stay-at-home mom. She is married to Andrew Dumm and has two children with him (along with a plethora of pets). In the interview, she expands on her personal views of the COVID-19 pandemic and the government response to it. She goes on to describe her experiences as a parent during the pandemic, with emphasis on the emotional toll it took on her and the difficulties she had with distance learning.

ucldc_schema:description.item: This story was told by an Ethnic Studies educator from Los Angeles. This story discusses the narrator's educational experiences growing up and as an educator, and how her Chicana identity has influenced her experiences over time. In regards to her work, the narrator talks about California's Assembly Bill 101, which mandates ethnic studies as a graduation requirement for high schoolers, and her role in developing the curriculum and co-founding the Liberated Ethnic Studies Model Curriculum Coalition. This video is part 2 of 2.
This story includes two video recordings for the same interview, two transcripts to accompany each video file, and an abstract for the story.
Metadata creation for this item was supported through a Confronting Extremism Program awarded through the Office of Inclusive Excellence.
